title: Institutional Harm through Threshold Cascades
summary: Can a population of people not individually inclined to harm others nonetheless produce harmful collective outcomes, purely because of the institutional structure they inhabit? Social scientists have long argued yes, but existing accounts are largely qualitative and provide no precise condition distinguishing safe institutions from unsafe ones. We develop a threshold cascade model in which agents have positive activation thresholds, harmful behavior is irreversible, and the institution exerts both standing pressure and peer influence along a weighted network.
